theory.title: Past perfect and narrative tenses
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 002. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Past perfect and narrative tenses
examples: They had already discussed the issue.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 002 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. content.passage: The question of 004 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 004 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Passive forms and reporting
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 005. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Passive forms and reporting
patterns.pattern: be + past participle / it is reported that
examples: The proposal was approved after consultation.
It is widely believed that early support matters.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 005 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 005 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Conditionals and concession
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 006. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Conditionals and concession
examples: If access improves, participation will rise.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 006 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Modal deduction and speculation
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 007. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Modal deduction and speculation
patterns.pattern: must / may / might / can't have + participle
examples: The figures must have been updated.
The delay might have been caused by the weather.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 007 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 007 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 008 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Inversion and cleft sentences
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 009. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Inversion and cleft sentences
examples: Not only did the policy reduce costs, but it also improved access.
What matters most is reliable evidence.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 009 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 009 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Hedging and advanced linking
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 010. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Hedging and advanced linking
patterns.pattern: tend to / arguably / nevertheless / to some extent
examples: The proposal seems to address the main concern.
Arguably, context matters more than first impressions.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.
